purpose: The Master role's own identity: which node this role runs as, where it sits on the overlay, and what it holds. This is a description of the ROLE, not a grant of authority. Read the election block before concluding this node is Master.
role_note: 'peer' is deliberate and load-bearing, and it contradicts Step 1 of the build plan, which asked for 'role: master' here. Step 1 predates Step 13. Under the elected model a Master IS a peer that won a unanimous election, so the identity on disk says peer and carries no claim to authority; contracts/consensus-protocol.md decides who is Master, and no manifest, directory name or bundle destination may decide it. tests/test_contracts.py::test_a_node_declares_itself_peer_until_it_is_elected fails this file if it drifts to 'master'. What 'master' names here is the ROLE this subvault implements — the node that signs — and that is recorded in role_implemented_by rather than in the identity.
role_implemented_by: master-node — the subvault implementing the signing role. A description of scope, not a grant.
overlay_note: 10.100.0.1 is the Master's anchor address in contracts/overlay.json. It is reserved for the signing role and no peer may take it.
capabilities_note: The same vocabulary a peer holds. The Master's powers are NOT in this list — cluster-vote is a say, not a grant, and signing comes from key possession rather than from a capability any manifest can confer. See ../contracts/capabilities.json.

operational_key.held: only when an elected cluster trust root names this node
operational_key.public_half_published_to: the elected cluster trust root's master_pubkey, which is where peers read it from
operational_key.note: Generating this key does not make this node Master, and this file does not record that it was generated. Step 1 of the build plan lands the keypair; election lands the authority. See ../contracts/consensus-protocol.md and security/key-management.md.

election.elects_itself_note: A node may vote for itself. It may not install itself: that needs every member's signature (one per member of the pair or trio) on a cluster trust root naming this node's operational public key. Nothing on disk can shortcut this.
election.authority_path: $SPARKNET_STATE_DIR/trust-root.json -> verified by services/sparknet-signer.py at start -> its root_id is recorded in every signature this node ever issues
